stories.headline: Canada and U.S. navigate tense trade talks as Trump signals potential deal
stories.summary: U.S. President Donald Trump indicated his administration is working toward a fair trade agreement with Canada, while a senior adviser continued to direct sharp rhetoric toward Ottawa. Meanwhile, Canada-U.S. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc briefed an economic advisory committee following U.S. midterm election shifts. The negotiations come amid broader pressures over potential cross-border tariffs and economic alignment.

stories.headline: Indian national sentenced to 19 years in U.S. murder-for-hire plot
stories.summary: An Indian national, Nikhil Gupta, was sentenced in New York to more than 19 years in prison for orchestrating a contract killing targeting Sikh activist Gurpatwant Pannun. U.S. and Canadian authorities noted the thwarted assassination attempt was closely linked to wider transnational repression efforts, including the fatal shooting of a Canadian Sikh activist in British Columbia. Gupta had previously pleaded guilty to murder-for-hire and conspiracy charges.

stories.headline: Supreme Court sets date for landmark ruling on Quebec secularism law
stories.summary: The Supreme Court of Canada announced it will release its long-awaited decision on Quebec's secularism law, Bill 21, on November 27. The constitutional challenge examines the limits of provincial authority to preemptively invoke the Charter's notwithstanding clause to shield legislation from judicial review. The ruling will carry sweeping national ramifications for civil liberties and the balance between provincial sovereignty and fundamental freedoms.

stories.headline: Supreme Court rules sexual assault victims are not required to communicate non-consent
stories.summary: In a pair of decisions, the Supreme Court of Canada affirmed that victims of sexual assault are under no legal obligation to verbally or physically communicate an absence of consent. The top court overturned a lower court finding that had improperly demanded proof that a complainant conveyed her refusal. The ruling sharpens the legal definition of affirmative consent in Canadian criminal law.

stories.headline: First Nations groups and NDP demand changes to federal major projects legislation
stories.summary: New Democrats and Indigenous youth advocates are pushing back against the federal government's proposed major projects legislation, warning it infringes upon treaty rights. First Nations youth announced plans for a national day of action next month to demonstrate against the bill. Critics argue the proposed statutory changes bypass proper consultation and take a paternalistic approach to resource development.

stories.headline: Ontario education unions secure strike mandates ahead of central bargaining
stories.summary: Five unions representing more than 250,000 teachers and school support staff have voted in favour of strike action across Ontario. Central contract bargaining is scheduled to start before the end of the month, raising the prospect of classroom disruptions if negotiations stall. Union leaders are seeking improved wages and working conditions in upcoming talks with the provincial government.

stories.headline: Ottawa and Ontario press Stellantis over proposed sale of Brampton plant
stories.summary: Federal officials revealed that automaker Stellantis could be forced to repay $831 million in government support if it proceeds with selling its Brampton assembly plant. Ontario Premier Doug Ford described closed-door talks with company and federal officials as challenging but productive, while urging Ottawa to eliminate industrial carbon pricing to keep the facility viable. The plant's prospective sale to defence contractor Roshel has stoked concerns over manufacturing jobs in the province.

stories.headline: Ontario Liberals wrap up leadership race to choose new party leader
stories.summary: Ontario Liberals are selecting their third leader since 2018 following a lengthy contest among candidates Navdeep Bains, Lee Fairclough, Stephanie Bowman, and Dylan Marando. The party hopes the vote will end years in the political wilderness and establish a viable alternative to Premier Doug Ford's majority government. Outgoing interim leader John Fraser noted that his primary role was paving the way for succession and rebuilding party momentum.

stories.headline: Ontario and Ottawa announce $250-million funding for new Sault Ste. Marie port
stories.summary: The federal and Ontario governments have each committed $125 million toward constructing a multimodal marine port in Sault Ste. Marie by 2031. Officials stated the project will expand cargo capacity, boost regional supply chains, and decrease Canadian trade reliance on American shipping channels. Local leaders described the announcement as a transformative investment for the northern economy.

stories.headline: Ontario finalizes regulations allowing school board directors to reject trustee motions
stories.summary: New provincial regulations grant unelected school board directors the authority to veto motions introduced by democratically elected trustees. The Ford government says the measures are intended to maintain administrative focus on core academic outcomes. Education advocates and governance experts criticized the decision, warning it erodes local democratic accountability.

stories.headline: United States slaps sanctions on alleged GTA faction of Italian mafia
stories.summary: The U.S. Department of the Treasury has sanctioned six alleged Canadian leaders of the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate alongside several businesses in the Greater Toronto Area. The targeted operations include local funeral homes accused of laundering illicit revenues and supporting organized crime activities. Law enforcement agencies on both sides of the border continue to target the international financial footprint of southern Ontario mob networks.

stories.headline: Major construction to snarl King Street West traffic and transit until 2027
stories.summary: The City of Toronto and the TTC are launching extensive infrastructure work along King Street West that will persist through winter 2027. The project entails replacing aging underground watermains and repairing streetcar tracks between Dufferin Street and Close Avenue. Commuters face lane reductions, intersection shutdowns, and streetcar diversions for more than a year.
